newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares establishing records at opening.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares establishing records at opening.

text.p: Russian shares surged to new records at opening on Tuesday as Russian and foreign investors lunged for second-tier shares and some leading stocks such as utility UES, traders said.
Many saw no end to the demand for the day and said investors were buying stock as it became available.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share index opened at a record 305.70, up from Monday's closing 304.90.
UES EESR.RTS broke through the 20 cent barrier and at 0905 GMT traded at $0.2000 after $0.1955 at Monday's close.

The two leaders were second-tier shares. Regional telecom MGTS MGTS.RTS jumped to $11.50 from $9.75 on 27,500 shares turnover. Novosibirskenergo NVNG.RTS utility jumped to $5.20 on two trades from $4.07 when it last traded, February 6.
"Momentum is starting to build," said ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko. "Like last year, no one wants to admit that the rally is here, because not everyone is loaded with stock."
Russian shares establishing records =2

"I thought there would be resistance at 15 cents (for UES), then 16, now 20, but there is still demand for almost everything," said Kirill Maltsev, institutional sales manager at Rye, Man and Gore Securities.
But he said that some investors who had bought the shares at eight cents were quietly taking profit.
"Any normal person would expect a fall in his gut, but on the other hand, the end is not visible."
Traders said that Russians, including some operators moving from the government securities market, were battling foreigners for paper as both tried to become invested.
"The orders are not as price sensitive these days," Kizenko said. "That shows a different kind of money."
